      "text": "\n\n\nThe best part about osu! web pages is that you don\u0027t actually need to scrape the messy HTML layout (divs, classes, etc.) to get the data. At the very bottom of the source code you provided, there is a hidden `\u003cscript\u003e` block with the ID `json-events`. This block contains all the data you see on the page—players, beatmaps, match results, combos, accuracy, and timestamps—in perfectly structured **JSON format**.\n\nHere is a lightweight Python script that doesn\u0027t require any external libraries. You can put this in the same folder as your `.html` file(s), run it, and it will strip away 95% of the useless HTML bloat, leaving you with a perfectly readable JSON file for the AI.\n\n### `osu_parser.py`\n\n```python\nimport json\nimport glob\nimport os\n\ndef parse_osu_html():\n    # Find all HTML files in the current folder\n    html_files \u003d glob.glob(\"*.html\")\n    \n    if not html_files:\n        print(\"No HTML files found in the current directory.\")\n        return\n\n    for file_path in html_files:\n        with open(file_path, \"r\", encoding\u003d\"utf-8\") as f:\n            content \u003d f.read()\n            \n            # Locate the hidden JSON data embedded by the osu! website\n            start_tag \u003d \u0027\u003cscript id\u003d\"json-events\" type\u003d\"application/json\"\u003e\u0027\n            end_tag \u003d \u0027\u003c/script\u003e\u0027\n            \n            start_idx \u003d content.find(start_tag)\n            \n            if start_idx !\u003d -1:\n                start_idx +\u003d len(start_tag)\n                end_idx \u003d content.find(end_tag, start_idx)\n                \n                if end_idx !\u003d -1:\n                    json_str \u003d content[start_idx:end_idx].strip()\n                    try:\n                        # Parse and format the JSON beautifully\n                        json_data \u003d json.loads(json_str)\n                        out_name \u003d os.path.splitext(file_path)[0] + \"_parsed.json\"\n                        \n                        with open(out_name, \"w\", encoding\u003d\"utf-8\") as out_f:\n                            json.dump(json_data, out_f, indent\u003d4, ensure_ascii\u003dFalse)\n                            \n                        print(f\"✅ Successfully extracted data from \u0027{file_path}\u0027 into \u0027{out_name}\u0027\")\n                    except json.JSONDecodeError:\n                        print(f\"❌ Found the tag in \u0027{file_path}\u0027, but failed to parse it as JSON.\")\n                else:\n                    print(f\"❌ Found start tag but no end tag in \u0027{file_path}\u0027.\")\n            else:\n                print(f\"⚠️ No \u0027json-events\u0027 tag found in \u0027{file_path}\u0027. (Are you sure this is an osu! room history page?)\")\n\nif __name__ \u003d\u003d \"__main__\":\n    parse_osu_html()\n```\n\n### How to use it:\n1. Save your osu! page as an `.html` file in a folder (for example, `match.html`).\n2. Create a new text file in the same folder, paste the code above into it, and save it as `osu_parser.py`.\n3. Open your terminal or command prompt, navigate to that folder, and run:\n   ```bash\n   python osu_parser.py\n   ```\n4. It will instantly generate a new file named `match_parsed.json`.\n\n### Why this is perfect for AI:\nInstead of forcing the AI to navigate through megabytes of `\u003cdiv\u003e` tags, UI images, navigation bars, and styling blocks, the output file will just look exactly like an API response:\n```json\n{\n    \"beatmaps\": [...],\n    \"room\": {\n        \"id\": 2657004,\n        \"name\": \"BPM vs. the World || 7*| FS, RR | W9\",\n        \"type\": \"team_versus\"\n    },\n    \"playlist_items\":[\n        {\n            \"beatmap_id\": 3970329,\n            \"scores\":[\n                 { \"user_id\": 34706005, \"accuracy\": 0.991424, \"total_score\": 75084 }\n            ]\n        }\n    ]\n}\n```",
